footer.disclaimer: XcodeSentinel is not an official Anthropic or Apple product. It does not bypass or extend any usage limit.

common.notOfficial: Not affiliated with Anthropic or Apple. "Xcode" and "Claude" are trademarks of their respective owners.
common.noBypass: XcodeSentinel does not bypass, extend, or work around usage limits. It only resumes your own session after a limit has already cleared.
common.xcodeOnly: Scope is Xcode's built-in Claude integration only. The VS Code extension and the Claude Code CLI already have official auto-continue, so they are out of scope.
common.noAppStore: Not distributed on the Mac App Store: an app that drives another app through the Accessibility API cannot ship in the App Sandbox. Downloads come from GitHub Releases only.
common.signed: Builds are signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

index.pageTitle: Keep your Xcode Claude sessions moving
index.pageDescription: A macOS menu-bar app that watches the Claude coding session inside Xcode and resumes it automatically when it stalls.
index.heroTitle: Keep your Xcode Claude sessions moving
index.heroLead: A macOS menu-bar utility that watches the Claude coding session inside Xcode and resumes it automatically when it stalls — so it isn't left idle for hours while you're away.
index.problemBody:
When you have Claude writing code inside Xcode and you step away, the session can sit stopped for hours:

  • the 5-hour rolling usage limit was hit,
  • the weekly limit was hit,
  • output was long and it is waiting on “Continue”.

You don't notice while you're out, and it stays stopped even after the limit resets.
index.solutionBody:
• Watches each registered Xcode window's Claude panel via the Accessibility API (no screenshots, no OCR).
  • When a limit clears, resumes your own session — one target at a time, paced, in priority order.
  • Notifies you (locally and via an optional webhook) so you can see what happened from your phone.
index.featuresBody:
State detection
Idle / working / awaiting-continue / session-limited / weekly-limited / awaiting-approval / awaiting-answer / errored — driven by editable patterns.
Safe auto-resume
One retry per stall (two if it recurs for the same reason), a daily cap, cooldowns, and a Dry-run mode.
Resume scheduler
Priority queue, one-at-a-time by default, spacing between starts, Quiet Hours.
Away notifications
Generic webhook with ntfy / Pushover / Discord / Slack presets. Target name, state and time only.
AX Inspector
Dump a window's Accessibility tree to JSON for bug reports and regression tests.
Never guesses
If the state can't be determined, it notifies and does nothing — it never sends into an unknown state.
index.requirementsBody:
• macOS 15 or later
  • Xcode with the Claude integration
  • Accessibility permission (explained on the Privacy page)
index.otherProjectsBody: See the portfolio hub for other apps and tools.

gettingStarted.pageDescription: Install XcodeSentinel and register your first Xcode target.
gettingStarted.heading: Getting started
gettingStarted.installBody:
1. Download the latest .dmg from GitHub Releases.
  2. Open the DMG and drag XcodeSentinel to Applications.
  3. Launch it. It lives in the menu bar (no Dock icon).
gettingStarted.gatekeeperBody: The build is signed with a Developer ID and notarized, so a normal double-click works. If macOS still blocks it, right-click the app → Open → Open, once.
gettingStarted.permissionBody: On first run the app asks for Accessibility permission and opens System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Enable XcodeSentinel there. Screen Recording is not requested.
gettingStarted.targetBody:
1. Open Settings → Targets → Add Target…
  2. Pick a running Xcode window from the list.
  3. Give it a display name and a resume prompt (default: “Please continue from where you stopped.”).
  4. Press Test Detection to confirm the Claude panel is found before you rely on it.
gettingStarted.dryRunBody: For the first day, enable Dry-run (Settings → Scheduler). Detection runs normally but nothing is sent — the log records what would have been sent. Turn it off once you trust the detection.
gettingStarted.screenshotsNote: Screenshots are added with the first tagged release.

guide.pageDescription: Every feature: targets, detection patterns, the scheduler, Quiet Hours, and webhook notifications.
guide.heading: Guide
guide.targetsBody: A target is one monitored Xcode window. It is stored by workspace path and display name, and re-bound to a live window on each launch (a restarted Xcode changes its PID). Per-target settings: priority, resume prompt, daily auto-resume cap, minimum interval between resumes, notify-on-stall, and whether destructive stops need manual approval.
guide.detectionBody: The state is read from Accessibility text, matched against rules in Patterns.json (editable in Settings, no rebuild needed). Each rule has anyOf / allOf / noneOf substrings, an optional role constraint, and an enabled flag. The first matching rule wins, so specific rules (weekly limit) precede general ones (session limit). “Test Detection” shows the resolved state plus any rules that nearly matched.
guide.schedulerBody: Targets that become resume-eligible are queued, not run immediately. The queue is ordered by priority then by how long the target has been stalled. Defaults: one resume in flight at a time (up to 3), 90 seconds between starts. Limit states are held until their reset time before dispatch.
guide.quietHoursBody: Set a window (e.g. 23:00–07:00) during which the app notifies but never resumes. Windows that cross midnight are handled.
guide.safetyBody:
• One automatic resume per stall; a second only if the stall recurs for the same reason; stop and notify on the third.
  • Daily cap per target (default 12).
  • Cooldown between resumes (default 120 s).
  • No auto-response to approval prompts or to questions Claude asks — notify only.
  • Dry-run: detect only, never send.
guide.webhookBody: Set an endpoint URL and pick a preset (ntfy / Pushover / Discord / Slack) or a custom JSON template with {{title}}, {{message}}, {{timestamp}}. The payload contains only the target's display name, the state, and a timestamp — never chat text or source code.
guide.axInspectorBody: Debug → AX Inspector shows the selected window's Accessibility tree with role / title / value / identifier, highlights the matching pattern, and exports the tree as JSON. Attach that JSON to bug reports (after checking it contains no real project names or paths).

troubleshooting.pageDescription: Detection failures, lost permission, Xcode updates, and using the AX Inspector.
troubleshooting.heading: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.detectionBody:
1. Open Debug → AX Inspector and dump the target window's tree.
  2. If the Claude panel elements aren't visible, the panel may be a separate window — re-add the target.
  3. If the text is present but the wording changed, update Patterns.json in Settings → Detection.
  4. After three consecutive “unknown” results the app pauses monitoring and notifies. Fix the cause, then resume.
troubleshooting.permissionBody: Re-signing the app or an OS update can drop the permission. The app detects this and notifies. Re-enable XcodeSentinel under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
troubleshooting.xcodeTitle: Detection broke after an Xcode update
troubleshooting.xcodeBody: Xcode's Claude-panel Accessibility structure is private and can change between versions. Most cases are fixed by updating Patterns.json. If the structure itself changed, file an issue with an AX Inspector dump attached.
troubleshooting.noResumeBody: This is often intended. The app never auto-resumes on awaitingApproval, awaitingUserAnswer, unknown, or errored. Otherwise check: the daily cap, the cooldown, the per-stall retry limit, Dry-run mode, and Quiet Hours.
troubleshooting.weeklyBody: The weekly limit does not reset after 5 hours. On weeklyLimited the app switches to a long wait (re-checks about every 30 minutes) and notifies.
troubleshooting.webhookBody: Check the endpoint URL and template in Settings → Notifications. The presets (ntfy / Pushover / Discord / Slack) fill in the format for you.

privacy.pageDescription: What XcodeSentinel reads, what it sends, and what it never sends.
privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.readsBody: Through the Accessibility API, for windows you register: element roles, titles, values, identifiers, and hierarchy of the Claude panel. This is how it detects the session state and finds the input field and Send button.
privacy.sendsBody:
• Local macOS notifications: target name, state, next action.
  • Optional webhook (only if you configure one): target display name, state, timestamp.
privacy.neverBody:
• Chat contents.
  • Source code or file contents.
  • Real file paths or project names in webhook payloads.

Detailed debug logging that could include more is opt-in and off by default. Logs never record chat text by default.
privacy.permsBody:
• Accessibility — required, for the above.
  • Screen Recording — not used. No screenshots, no OCR.
privacy.networkBody: No analytics, no tracking, no telemetry. The only outbound request is the webhook you configure, to the URL you provide.

faq.pageDescription: Common questions about scope, limits, App Store distribution, and safety.
faq.heading: FAQ
faq.q1: Does this get around the usage limit?
faq.a1: No. It does not bypass, extend, or work around any limit. It resumes your own session after a limit has already cleared, and it will not keep sending during a limit.
faq.q2: Why Xcode only? What about VS Code or the Claude Code CLI?
faq.a2: Claude Code already has an official “Continue automatically at usage limit” setting (on by default), and the VS Code extension is built on Claude Code, so it inherits that. Xcode's Claude integration is an Apple IDE feature on a separate track and has no equivalent — that gap is why this app exists.
faq.q3: Why isn't it on the Mac App Store?
faq.a3: It drives another app (Xcode) through the Accessibility API, which is not possible inside the App Sandbox that the App Store requires. It is distributed via GitHub Releases as a signed, notarized DMG.
faq.q4: Is it safe to run unattended?
faq.a4: It is built to fail safe: it never acts on an unknown state, never answers approval prompts or questions, caps retries and daily resumes, and has a Dry-run mode. Even so, review the safety settings and start in Dry-run.
faq.q5: Does it work for the weekly limit?
faq.a5: It detects the weekly limit, switches to a long wait, and notifies. It cannot make the weekly limit reset sooner.
faq.q6: Is this made by Anthropic or Apple?
faq.a6: No. It is an independent tool. “Xcode” and “Claude” are trademarks of their respective owners.
